description: RIFT CMB full CLASS external_Pk injection. Fixes referee vulnerability 3: prior C_ell used first-order modulation approximation. Now derives P(k) from RIFT growth factor D_RIFT(z)/D_LCDM(z) via G_eff(Psi) and modified H(z), injects as CLASS external_Pk, runs full Boltzmann transfer function.

rift_params.note: Best-fit from SIM87 full-cov BAO refit (2026-04-07)

growth.interpretation: R < 1 means RIFT suppresses structure growth relative to LCDM (G_eff < G in Psi-populated regions). This reduces sigma_8 and suppresses ISW.

external_Pk.note: RIFT P(k) = LCDM P(k) * R_growth^2 (scale-independent growth correction)

class_results.chi2_interpretation: Full-sky noise-free Gaussian chi2 = sum_l (2l+1)/2 * [x-1-ln(x)] where x = C_l^RIFT/C_l^LCDM. This is NOT chi2 vs Planck data. The large value (423) is expected for a 3% RMS deviation summed over 1500 modes without noise (per-mode contribution = 0.34). The actual Planck likelihood comparison requires the Planck likelihood code and is beyond the scope of this simulation. The quantity reported here measures the theoretical signal-to-noise of the RIFT vs LCDM difference, not observational distinguishability.
class_results.dominant_effect: The 2.93% RMS deviation is driven by the shifted BAO best-fit cosmological parameters (H0=68.14 vs 67.36, Omega_m=0.294 vs 0.315), not G_eff (D_RIFT/D_LCDM=1.000000 to 6 d.p.). The effect enters through: (1) different angular diameter distance to last scattering -> peak positions shift, (2) different expansion history -> ISW, (3) different Omega_m -> early ISW and lensing.

verdict.note: RIFT CMB is a 2.93% RMS perturbation on LCDM across l=2-1500. Full CLASS Boltzmann treatment is now used — the first-order approximation is superseded. G_eff growth effect is negligible (R=1.000000); the dominant RIFT CMB signal is from the shifted H0/Omega_m background (BAO best-fit). A proper Planck likelihood comparison is Phase 5b (beyond this simulation).
